first of all, use a detached LUKs header. LUKs is helper information for dm-crypt. Without the header attached to the partition, the data is as if you used dm-crypt (with the same configuration that is. Second of all carefully partitioned, but whose partitions look entirely random is also easily over come. My internal SSD has only one partition, and no GPT. There isn't even the data that says theres any partitions. First byte to last byte is my partition, and thus totally encrypted.

As for boot drive, im not sure if you're talking about \boot or EFI partition. In my case I had combined them as its easier managed when using UEFI. My EFI partition contains my kernel, which is combined with EFIbootstub support, meaning I don't need a bootloader, and I don't need a \boot partition.

I don't quite understand your problem with flash as a boot device, its quite simple, and since my kernel and initramFS is only 12MB, im not hitting any transferspeed limit on a quality USB3.0 device/port. Even a cheap USB should bottle neck at only 12MB.

as for the last part about fiddly repair mode: you can use efibootmgr to set your default (and only) boot device to be your USB drive, meaning you can boot your computer with a press of a button, without doing any boot repair or going into BIOS settings.
